jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager, Infrastructure, Scaling & Core Workflow Primitives



Transform healthcare with us.

At Qualified Health, we're redefining what's possible with Generative AI in healthcare. Our infrastructure provides the guardrails for safe AI governance, healthcare-specific agent creation, and real-time algorithm monitoring, working alongside leading health systems to drive real change.

This is more than just a job. It's an opportunity to build the future of AI in healthcare, solve complex challenges, and make a lasting impact on patient care. If you're ambitious, innovative, and ready to move fast, we'd love to have you on board.




JOB SUMMARY

Qualified Health is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own how the platform compounds: the core workflow primitives that every product is assembled from, the builder tools that let teams create assistants, abstractors, and workflows, and the scaling discipline that turns one-off builds into products that generalize. Builder tools are the velocity engine of our platform. This role makes the engine compound: a component built once for one application becomes a primitive available to every application after it.

This is a three-prong role. First, identify and productize the scalable primitives: the triggers, ingestion patterns, extraction steps, review gates, and serving patterns that recur across products, so they are built once, versioned, and reused everywhere. Second, make sure products ship scalable, not as one-offs: generalization requirements are set before build, and the second customer costs a fraction of the first. Third, drive the builder tools themselves: the roadmap for Workflow Factory and its sibling builders, and the runtime underneath them, including registries, config-driven backends, and the path from a built workflow to production.

You are not the infrastructure owner. Engineering owns the runtime, the architecture, and their technical decisions. You are the scalability partner: the person who has written down what must generalize, who catches the one-off before it ships, and who owns the product definition of the primitives and the tools that assemble them.

Your success is measured by reuse. If the second product built on a primitive takes as long as the first, the role has failed.

You will sit on the Platform pod, reporting to the SVP of Product, and partner daily with engineering leadership, the Workflow Factory team, the data and analytics product manager, and peer product managers.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

You own products, catalogs, and requirements. Engineering owns the domains.

 - Core workflow primitives as a product: The catalog of shared components that workflows, assistants, and abstractors are assembled from. Each primitive is defined once, versioned, discoverable, and stable enough that engineering can refactor underneath without breaking the products built on top. You own what exists in the catalog, its interfaces, and its adoption.

 - The promotion path from one-off to primitive: The intake, criteria, and process for when a component built for one application gets promoted into the shared catalog, who migrates to it, and how deprecation works. Pattern recognition across products is the core skill of this role.

 - Builder tools: The co-own product roadmap for Workflow Factory, Assistant Builder, and Abstractor Builder: what builders can create, what guardrails apply, and what it takes to go from built to deployed in production.

 - The builder tools runtime as a product surface: Registries, config-driven backends, and the pipeline that ships a built workflow to production, including automated review gates. Engineering owns the implementation; you own the requirements, the interfaces, and the roadmap.

 - Scalability and generalization requirements: The non-negotiables written before any new product build starts: multi-tenancy, configuration over code, performance at full population scale, and reuse of existing primitives. You partner with infrastructure engineering to make these real; you do not let a bespoke build reach a second customer.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the roadmap for builder tools and core primitives, balancing customer commitments, internal builder needs, and platform reuse

 - Build and maintain the primitive catalog: what exists, its interface, its version, and who consumes it

 - Define and run the promotion process that turns per-customer builds into reusable platform components with clear interfaces

 - Set generalization and scalability requirements at the start of every new product build, and enforce them at review gates

 - Write complete acceptance criteria before work commits to a sprint; no ambiguity reaches engineering

 - Own product requirements for the workflow registry, config-driven backends, and the build-to-production pipeline, in partnership with the Workflow Factory team

 - Partner with infrastructure engineering on multi-tenancy, performance, reliability, and cost as product requirements, not afterthoughts

 - Define success metrics for reuse and platform leverage (component adoption, time-to-second-deployment, share of new products assembled from existing primitives) and use them to drive prioritization

 - Run intake and prioritization for builder tool asks from customer teams and internal builders

 - Navigate healthcare regulatory requirements (HIPAA, data privacy, clinical safety) as first-order product constraints




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelors Degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field

 - 6+ years of product management experience, with 3+ years owning platform, developer tools, or infrastructure products

 - Demonstrated pattern recognition across products: you have taken capabilities built for one customer or team and turned them into shared components others adopted

 - Deep technical fluency: you can go toe-to-toe with engineers on workflow orchestration, APIs, event-driven architectures, and config-driven systems, and you can read a schema and follow a codebase

 - Experience with builder tools, low-code platforms, internal developer platforms, or component libraries at scale

 - Experience shipping products in regulated environments (healthcare, finance, or similar)

 - Excellent communication skills: you can explain platform tradeoffs to executives and product requirements to engineers, and you can influence teams you do not manage

 - Comfort with ambiguity and ability to make decisions with incomplete information

 - Able to work onsite in Palo Alto 3 days/week

Bonus: Understanding of healthcare operations or health system IT environments; experience with workflow engines (Temporal or similar), LLM agent frameworks, or design systems and component governance.




WHY JOIN QUALIFIED HEALTH?

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing company and a world-class team that is poised to change the healthcare industry. We are a passionate, mission-driven team building a category-defining product. We are backed by premier investors and are looking for team members excited to do the best work of their careers.

Our employees are integral to achieving our goals, so we are proud to offer competitive salaries with equity packages, robust medical/dental/vision insurance, flexible working hours, hybrid work options, and an inclusive environment that fosters creativity and innovation.




OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY

Qualified Health is an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is essential to our success, and we are committed to building a team that reflects the world we live in. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

Pay & Benefits: The pay range for this role is $170,000 - $200,000 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. This role is also eligible for equity and benefits.

Join our mission to revolutionize healthcare with AI. To apply, please send your resume through the application below.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
TRANSFORM HEALTHCARE WITH US.

At Qualified Health, we're redefining what's possible with Generative AI in healthcare. Our infrastructure provides the guardrails for safe AI governance, healthcare-specific agent creation, and real-time algorithm monitoring—working alongside leading health systems to drive real change.

This is more than just a job. It's an opportunity to build the future of AI in healthcare, solve complex challenges, and make a lasting impact on patient care. If you're ambitious, innovative, and ready to move fast, we'd love to have you on board.

Join us in shaping the future of healthcare.




JOB SUMMARY:

The Product Manager will own our denials and appeals product — one of three products under our Medical Necessity umbrella, alongside Utilization Review and a peer-to-peer tool — as it grows across a widening set of health system clients and use cases. This is an ownership seat: you will decide what gets built, for whom, and in what order, and you will be accountable for whether it works when a real utilization review nurse sits down in front of it.

You will develop requirements directly with customers, partner with engineering and design to turn them into shipped software, and stay close enough to live deployments to know whether what you built actually landed. We are looking for someone who has built AI products before, not someone who has managed a roadmap adjacent to one — the hard problems here are specific to this kind of work: what to do when the model is right most of the time, how much to show a clinician before you have earned their trust, where the human belongs in the loop, and how you know any of it is working. This position requires deep comfort operating in Jira, real product judgment under ambiguity, and genuine curiosity about how care gets authorized, denied, and appealed.





KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Own the denials and appeals product end to end — discovery, requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration

 - Define what good looks like for an AI feature in a clinical and financial workflow: accuracy thresholds, human review points, failure behavior, and the production metrics that prove it works

 - Manage the day-to-day interaction between customers, design, and engineering: translate requests into clear, buildable work with real acceptance criteria

 - Own prioritization across competing customer needs, and the reasoning behind each call

 - Take features from zero to one — shape the concept, get something real in front of customers fast, and iterate on what you learn

 - Feed patterns back into the roadmap: when three customers ask for the same thing, be the person who noticed

 - Coordinate with the teams owning Utilization Review and the peer-to-peer tool so the Medical Necessity products feel like one coherent suite




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree

 - 3+ years in product management, owning a product or a substantial product area end to end

 - Demonstrated experience shipping a real product to a real customer: you owned something from early stage through to a customer using it in production and continuing to use it. School projects and internships do not count here

 - Demonstrable experience building AI products. You have shipped something where the model was central to the product, and you can speak specifically to what you learned when it did not behave the way you expected

 - Customer-facing experience developing requirements directly with customers, not through an intermediary

 - Direct experience working with engineering and design teams — writing up requirements, managing a backlog, driving delivery against a sprint cadence

 - Deep comfort with Jira as your primary working tool

 - Excellent written and verbal communication; able to hold a thread across multiple customers and internal teams at once

 - Able to work onsite in Palo Alto several days a week is strongly preferred, as the rest of the team is local. We will consider exceptional candidates elsewhere


IDEAL EXPERIENCE

 - Zero-to-one experience — you have led the launch of a new product or major product area, or been close enough to one to know how it actually goes

 - Healthcare domain knowledge, especially revenue cycle management, denials and appeals, prior authorization, or utilization review

 - Experience at a mid-size company — scope broad enough to own something real, organization structured enough to ship reliably

 - Exposure to enterprise or health system customers, and to the reality that every customer wants something slightly different

 - Familiarity with healthcare workflows, terminology, or health system IT environments

 - Genuine appetite to go deep on the utilization review and medical necessity domain

 - Familiarity with Linear and Notions




DESIRABLE SKILLS

 - Execution Bias: You would rather close ten things than debate one. You default to making the list and working the list

 - Builder Instincts: You reach for a prototype or a working example rather than a longer document. Deep vibe-coding skill is not required — our analysts handle much of the early build — but you think like someone who makes things

 - Ownership: Given an ambiguous customer request, you drive it to a decision rather than waiting for one

 - Cross-Functional Judgment: You can sit between a customer, a designer, and an engineer and make all three feel heard while still moving the work forward

 - Prioritization Instinct: When two customers want incompatible things in the same sprint, you can frame the tradeoff clearly enough for someone to decide

 - Learning Agility: You get to real fluency in a new clinical domain fast, and you ask good questions while you're getting there

 - Product Judgment: You can decide with incomplete information, say why you decided that way, and change your mind when the evidence moves




WHY JOIN QUALIFIED HEALTH?

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing company and a world-class team, that is poised to change the healthcare industry. We are a passionate, mission-driven team that is building a category-defining product. We are backed by premier investors and are looking for founding team members who are excited to do the best work of their careers.

Our employees are integral to achieving our goals so we are proud to offer competitive salaries with equity packages, robust medical/dental/vision insurance, flexible working hours, hybrid work options and an inclusive environment that fosters creativity and innovation.




OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY

Qualified Health is an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is essential to our success, and we are committed to building a team that reflects the world we live in. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, disability, or veteran status.



Pay & Benefits: The pay range for this role is between $110,000 - $140,000, and will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. This role is also eligible for equity and benefits.

Join our mission to revolutionize healthcare with AI. To apply, please send your resume through the application below.
